title: Binge Eating Disorder: More Than Just Overeating
description: BED is the most common eating disorder and highly treatable. What it is, how it differs from overeating, and evidence-based treatments that work.

content.text: Everyone overeats sometimes. But binge eating disorder is different—it's episodes of uncontrollable eating followed by shame and distress. It's the most common eating disorder, and it's treatable.

items: Eating unusually large amounts of food in a short period
Feeling out of control during the episode
Feeling disgusted, depressed, or guilty afterward

content.text: Episodes happen at least once a week for 3+ months.

items: Emotional eating without loss of control
Feeling unable to stop or control eating during episodes
Most common eating disorder (~3% of US adults)
Affects all genders (slightly more common in women)
History of dieting is a risk factor
CBT-E (Enhanced CBT for eating disorders) - most evidence
Focuses on triggers, emotions, eating patterns
SSRIs can help reduce binge frequency
GLP-1 drugs being studied (off-label use growing)
General weight loss programs (don't address the binge eating)

content.text: Weight loss should not be the primary treatment goal for BED. Addressing the binge eating comes first—weight often stabilizes when binging stops.

Binge eating disorder is not a willpower problem or just loving food too much. It's a recognized psychiatric condition with effective treatments. If you're struggling with loss of control around food, help is available—and it works.
